title: Pure stored-event upcaster
description: Objective: implement the pure stored-event schema-dispatch half of task-82989467aa474ae786f0c4eb8b23bfb0 without folding projection state. Deliverable: packages/store/src/projections/projection-upcast.ts, its one-line .js bridge, and focused tests for explicit per-event-type current versions, exact multi-hop routes keyed by (eventType, fromVersion), envelope preservation, and detached payload/metadata transformation. StoredEvent domainSchemaVersion values are opaque strings: no numeric/lexical future-version inference. NOT in scope: projection state/reducers, duplicate or ordering checks across event sequences, SQLite, transactions, persistence, quarantine, relay/inbox, CURSOR_GAP, root package export, or real business upcasters. Hard dependency: task-a602b3d4294a44aea1d9d173bf1fdaa7 is DONE and supplies StoredEvent.domainSchemaVersion. Owned paths: packages/store/src/projections/projection-upcast.ts, projection-upcast.js, projection-upcast.test.ts. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/store typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/store exec vitest run --root ../.. packages/store/src/projections/projection-upcast.test.ts.
definitionOfDone: An explicitly current version returns a detached frozen-envelope snapshot without invoking a handler, while registered legacy versions follow the exact acyclic multi-hop route to the declared current version.

Every upcast preserves eventId, aggregateId/sequence, globalPosition, command/request/record/codec/provenance fields and eventType; handlers may replace only payload and metadata, whose bytes are defensively copied.

An unregistered starting version returns frozen SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED evidence naming the offending event and declared current version; it is never treated as current, passed through successfully, or dropped.

Duplicate dispatch keys, duplicate event-type definitions, self-loops, cycles/dead ends, throwing/thenable handlers, and malformed handler output fail closed under frozen deterministic local codes with no partial successful event.

projection-upcast.ts is <=165 physical lines, projection-upcast.test.ts is <=220, the bridge is one exact re-export line, no production import or call reaches SQLite/transactions/clock/filesystem/randomness, and the focused verification command exits 0.

implementationPlan.description: TDD RED, part 1 of 2 — write the success-path tests in projection-upcast.test.ts. It will not compile yet; that is the expected red. Add a compact `storedEvent(overrides)` helper building a full StoredEvent (globalPosition: 1n, decisionTrace present in at least one fixture) and a `patch(payload, metadata)` helper. Cover: (a) an event whose domainSchemaVersion equals the declared currentVersion returns ok with NO handler invoked — assert a call-log array is empty; (b) an exact multi-hop route v1->v2->v3 with currentVersion v3 invokes handlers in exactly that order, asserted against a recorded call log, not a call count; (c) envelope preservation — assert Object.keys(result.event).sort().join(",") equals the same expression on the input event, and assert eventId, aggregateId, aggregateSequence, globalPosition (1n), commandId, committedAt, requestSha256, recordVersion, payloadCodecVersion, decisionTrace and eventType are each equal to the input; (d) the successful outcome's domainSchemaVersion equals the declared currentVersion, in BOTH the zero-hop and multi-hop cases — this is the field that is rewritten, not preserved; (e) detachment — result.payload.buffer !== input.payload.buffer and likewise for metadata, and mutating result bytes leaves the input bytes unchanged, in the zero-hop case too; (f) Object.isFrozen(result.event) is true while the byte arrays are deliberately NOT frozen; (g) opaque versions — register currentVersion "v9" with no route from "v10" and assert "v10" fails rather than being inferred as newer, proving no numeric or lexical ordering.
implementationPlan.note:
Success-path tests written; RED confirmed — `Error: Cannot find module './projection-upcast.js' imported from .../projection-upcast.test.ts` at :7. 4 tests, 136 lines.

All seven plan sub-items covered: (a) zero-hop asserts `log` is EMPTY — a call-log array, not a spy count; (b) multi-hop asserts `log` deep-equals `["v1->v2","v2->v3"]`, and the two routes are DECLARED IN REVERSE ORDER (v2->v3 before v1->v2) so array order cannot be mistaken for route order; payload/metadata byte accumulation `[1,2,3]`/`[9,8,2,3]` independently pins the hop sequence; (c) `Object.keys(result).sort().join(",")` vs the same on the input, plus a per-field loop over PRESERVED_KEYS (10 fields, `toBe` identity) with globalPosition re-asserted as `1n` and decisionTrace by `toEqual`; (d) domainSchemaVersion asserted equal to the DECLARED currentVersion in both the zero-hop ("v3") and hop ("v2"/"v3") cases; (e) `.buffer` inequality for both arrays plus a write-through probe — mutate `result.payload[0]`/`result.metadata[0]` to 99, assert the input still reads `[1,2,3]`/`[9,8]` — exercised in the zero-hop case where aliasing is likeliest; (f) `Object.isFrozen` true for the outcome AND the envelope, false for both byte arrays; (g) currentVersion "v9" with only a v8->v9 route, event at "v10" — asserts ok:false and an empty call log, so "v10 > v9" is neither inferred nor half-executed.

Two hardening choices beyond the plan, both cheap:
1. The pass-through case uses handler `(input) => input` — the handler hands its INPUT patch straight back, so the test fails if production copies bytes on only one side of the call. The plan's transform-style handlers would have hidden that by returning fresh arrays anyway.
2. `omitTrace()` builds a fixture with decisionTrace ABSENT (not undefined) and asserts the result's key set still matches. Under exactOptionalPropertyTypes a spread-based envelope rebuild must not materialize `decisionTrace: undefined`; without this the key-set assertion only ever sees the present-trace shape.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the type surface and the compile half of projection-upcast.ts. Single type-only import: `import type { StoredEvent } from "../store-contracts.js";`. Export UpcastPatch {payload, metadata: Uint8Array}; UpcastHandler = (input: UpcastPatch) => UpcastPatch; UpcastRoute {fromVersion, toVersion, handler}; UpcastDefinition {eventType, currentVersion, routes}; UpcastDefinitionCode = "UPCAST_DUPLICATE_EVENT_TYPE" | "UPCAST_DUPLICATE_DISPATCH_KEY" | "UPCAST_SELF_LOOP" | "UPCAST_ROUTE_CYCLE" | "UPCAST_ROUTE_DEAD_END"; class UpcastDefinitionError extends Error with a readonly code; UpcastFailureCode = "SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED" | "UPCAST_HANDLER_FAILED" | "UPCAST_OUTPUT_INVALID"; UpcastFailure {code, eventId, eventType, fromVersion, currentVersion: string | null}; UpcastOutcome = {ok:true, event:StoredEvent} | {ok:false, failure:UpcastFailure}; StoredEventUpcaster {upcast(event): UpcastOutcome}. Then implement compileStoredEventUpcaster(definitions): build a Map keyed by eventType holding {currentVersion, routes: Map<fromVersion, {toVersion, handler}>}, COPYING the caller's arrays into the internal Maps so later mutation of the input cannot affect dispatch. Reject a repeated eventType, a repeated fromVersion within one event type, and fromVersion === toVersion. Then prove reachability: because each fromVersion has at most one outgoing edge, walk from each fromVersion following toVersion with a visited Set — revisiting a version throws UPCAST_ROUTE_CYCLE, and reaching a version that is neither the currentVersion nor a registered fromVersion throws UPCAST_ROUTE_DEAD_END. Narrow every Map.get result with a real conditional; noUncheckedIndexedAccess forbids non-null assertions.
implementationPlan.note:
Type surface + compile half landed. `pnpm --filter @moe/store typecheck` exit 0. Focused suite: 9 passed / 9 failed of 18 — the passing 9 are exactly the compile-time and refusal paths this step owns (5 definition-invalid cases, both SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED cases, opaque-ordering, purity); the failing 9 all require the real dispatch loop that step 5 adds. 149 lines against the 165 cap.

Surface is as planned, with field order alphabetized inside each declaration to match the store package's existing convention.

Three deviations from the plan's letter, all deliberate:

1. NO `fail(): never` HELPER. The plan had `fail()` narrow `hop` to non-undefined via never-return control-flow analysis. That narrowing depends on TypeScript recognizing the callee as never-returning, which has real preconditions (explicit `never` annotation, callee resolved as a function declaration or const). `throw new UpcastDefinitionError(...)` at each site needs no such analysis — control flow after a `throw` is unreachable by the grammar, not by inference. Costs a few lines, removes a whole failure mode with noUncheckedIndexedAccess. Zero non-null assertions in the file.

2. THE REACHABILITY WALK STOPS AT currentVersion (`while (version !== currentVersion)`) rather than walking until the map lookup misses. This makes compile-time reachability model exactly what dispatch does at runtime. Consequence worth flagging for review: a stray route OUT of the current version (currentVersion "v2" with routes v1->v2 and v2->v3) compiles clean and is simply dead, instead of being reported UPCAST_ROUTE_DEAD_END. That is correct — the DoD enumerates exactly five definition defects and an unreachable extra route is not one of them — and it matches the runtime rule that such a route can never fire. The plan's walk-until-miss form would have rejected it under a code that does not describe it.

3. `refuse()` takes `fromVersion` EXPLICITLY rather than reading event.domainSchemaVersion. Post-compile, reachability is proven, so SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED can only ever fire on the FIRST hop — where the stalled version and the recorded version are identical, which is what the two DoD-pinned tests assert. The explicit parameter exists so step 5's handler failures can name the hop they stalled at instead of the original recorded version. Documented in the module header so a reviewer does not read `fromVersion` as "the event's stored version" unconditionally.

Header comment is prose-audited against the purity test: no `Date.now`, `Math.random`, `require(` or `import(` token, and no comment line begins with `import` (the test's /^\s*import\b/ scan would otherwise count it as a second import). That test already passes.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the dispatch half of projection-upcast.ts and add the one-line bridge, taking the suite green. upcast(event): resolve the definition for event.eventType — if absent, return the frozen SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED failure with currentVersion null. Copy bytes with `new Uint8Array(source)` — never .slice(), because Buffer.prototype.slice returns a shared view. Check "already at currentVersion" FIRST, before any route lookup, so the zero-hop case returns a detached snapshot with no handler invoked and a stray route out of the current version can never fire. Otherwise loop: look up the route for the current version, and on a miss return frozen SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED naming the offending event and the declared currentVersion; invoke the handler inside try/catch, mapping a throw to UPCAST_HANDLER_FAILED; test the returned value for a callable .then BEFORE checking its shape and map a thenable to UPCAST_HANDLER_FAILED without awaiting; then require a non-null object whose own keys are exactly payload and metadata with both instanceof Uint8Array, mapping anything else to UPCAST_OUTPUT_INVALID; copy both returned arrays and advance to the route's toVersion. On success build the envelope by spreading the original event and overriding only payload, metadata and domainSchemaVersion (set to the declared currentVersion), Object.freeze the envelope, the failure objects and the outcome objects, and never freeze a byte array — Object.freeze on a non-empty Uint8Array throws "Cannot freeze array buffer views with elements". No partial event may be constructed on any failure path. Then create projection-upcast.js containing exactly the single line `export * from "./projection-upcast.ts";`.
implementationPlan.note:
Dispatch half + bridge landed. Suite GREEN: 18/18. `pnpm --filter @moe/store typecheck` exit 0. Sizes: projection-upcast.ts 164 (cap 165), .test.ts 215 (cap 220), .js exactly 1 line.

Dispatch follows the plan's ordering exactly: unknown eventType refused with currentVersion null before anything else; `while (version !== currentVersion)` is the FIRST thing evaluated after the definition resolves, so the zero-hop case never reaches a route lookup and a stray route out of the current version can never fire; handler invoked inside try/catch; thenable tested BEFORE shape; both returned arrays copied before advancing to hop.toVersion. Every byte copy is `new Uint8Array(source)` — `.slice()` appears nowhere in the file (Buffer.prototype.slice aliases). The success envelope is `{ ...event, domainSchemaVersion: currentVersion, metadata, payload }`, so exactly three fields are overridden and decisionTrace's presence or absence rides through the spread untouched. Object.freeze is applied to the envelope, the failure, and both outcome objects, and to no Uint8Array.

ONE STRUCTURAL DEVIATION: the plan specified two predicates (`isThenable` then `isPatch`); I shipped a single `checkOutput(value): UpcastPatch | "UPCAST_HANDLER_FAILED" | "UPCAST_OUTPUT_INVALID"`. Same checks in the same order — the merge was forced by the line cap, and it has a side benefit: the thenable-before-shape ordering is now impossible to reorder accidentally at the call site, because dispatch no longer contains two separately-movable `if` blocks. Null-safety detail worth a reviewer's eye: the `.then` probe is guarded by `couldThen` (object-and-not-null, or function), so `checkOutput(null)` short-circuits instead of dereferencing null.

SIZE WORK — this is the part most likely to be questioned, so the accounting is explicit. First green implementation was 192 lines, 27 over cap. Compressed in two passes to 164 with ZERO behavioural change: blank lines between type declarations removed; `Routes`/`Compiled`/`OutputCheck` aliases introduced so three multi-line signatures collapse to one line each; five `throw new UpcastDefinitionError(...)` sites routed through a 3-line `defect()` factory that returns the error for the call site to `throw` (returns the error rather than being a `never`-returning thrower, so no site depends on TypeScript's never-return control-flow narrowing); multi-line `if` conditions folded. No validation, branch, or error code was removed — the same 18 tests pass before and after, which is the evidence that the compression was behaviour-preserving.

Bridge is `export * from "./projection-upcast.ts";` matching store-digests.js byte-for-byte modulo the module name. Re-confirming step 4's finding: vitest resolves the `.js` specifier to `.ts` on its own, so no test in this package can detect a missing bridge — its correctness rests on convention review, not the suite.

API SHAPE (the one real design decision; reject the plan if you disagree):
Chosen — two-function seam: `compileStoredEventUpcaster(definitions)` THROWS a module-local `UpcastDefinitionError` (carrying a frozen `code`) for static wire-up defects, and the returned upcaster's `upcast(event)` RETURNS a frozen result union for per-event outcomes.
Why split: definition defects (duplicate keys, duplicate event types, self-loops, cycles, dead ends) have no event to attach evidence to, and are programmer wire-up bugs detected once at startup. Per-event failures must be recordable evidence because the parent fold task (task-82989467) needs to quarantine an offending event without a try/catch per event in its hot loop. DoD item 3 explicitly says the unsupported case *returns* evidence; DoD item 4 only requires definition defects to *fail closed under frozen codes*, which a thrown frozen code satisfies.
Rejected — one uniform evidence return for definition errors too: forces empty-string or nullable event-identity fields on a failure shape that has no event, and pushes the production file over its 165-line cap.
Rejected — throwing DurableStoreError with a new code: the task rail forbids extending DurableStoreErrorCode, and the union type makes it a typecheck failure anyway.
Rejected — validating definitions on every upcast call: re-does O(routes) work per event and duplicates the failure surface.

CYCLE/DEAD-END DETECTION: because duplicate dispatch keys are rejected, each (eventType, fromVersion) has at most one outgoing edge — a functional graph. So reachability of currentVersion is decidable at compile time by walking each fromVersion with a visited set. This makes dispatch a trivial bounded loop and is why no runtime hop counter is needed (see risks).

planningNotes.risks:
1. Object.freeze ON BYTES CRASHES. I ran it: `Object.freeze(new Uint8Array(2))` throws TypeError "Cannot freeze array buffer views with elements" (empty arrays freeze fine, so a naive deep-freeze passes tests with 0-byte fixtures and explodes on real data). Freeze the ENVELOPE OBJECT and the failure/outcome objects only. Never freeze payload/metadata. DoD says "frozen-envelope", not frozen bytes.
2. DO NOT COPY BYTES WITH .slice(). Node's Buffer is a Uint8Array subclass whose .slice() is an alias for .subarray() — it returns a VIEW sharing the same ArrayBuffer, so a Buffer-backed payload would silently fail the detachment requirement. Use `new Uint8Array(source)`, which copies into a fresh buffer from any Uint8Array or Buffer and normalizes the result to a plain Uint8Array.
3. domainSchemaVersion IS NOT PRESERVED — it is REWRITTEN to the declared currentVersion on every successful outcome, including the zero-hop case. DoD item 2 deliberately omits it from the preserved-field list. Preserving it is the most likely silent bug in this task.
4. PROSE-GREP TRAP (learned the hard way, see mem:gotcha-boundary-test-greps-prose-not-imports): the purity test reads the production file's raw text. Any forbidden token written in a COMMENT trips it exactly like real code. Keep the production file's comments free of the literal tokens `Date.now`, `Math.random`, `require(` and `import(`. Assert on the exact import-statement LIST rather than grepping for `sqlite`/`node:` substrings — that is the mutation-resistant form and it cannot be tripped by prose.
5. noUncheckedIndexedAccess makes every `map.get(...)` `T | undefined`. Narrow it with a real conditional; do not use `!`.
6. globalPosition is bigint — fixtures must use `1n`, and toEqual on a bigint mismatch is easy to miss if you write `1`.
7. No runtime hop guard is planned in the dispatch loop. That is safe ONLY because compile copies routes into an internal Map and proves every fromVersion reaches currentVersion, so a caller mutating their definitions array after compile cannot introduce a cycle. If you change compile to hold the caller's arrays by reference, you must add the guard.
8. Ordering matters in two places: dispatch checks "already at currentVersion" BEFORE any route lookup (so a stray route out of the current version can never fire), and the handler-output check tests thenable BEFORE shape (so a returned Promise reports UPCAST_HANDLER_FAILED, not UPCAST_OUTPUT_INVALID).
9. Line caps are DoD items, not guidance. If projection-upcast.ts exceeds 165, compress type declarations onto single lines — do NOT drop a validation. If the test exceeds 220, collapse the definition-invalid and output-invalid families into it.each tables.
10. Shared working directory: packages/scheduler/src/budget/ is currently untracked foreign work. Do not run a full-repo `pnpm test` and do not stage anything outside the three owned paths.
